key_insight: QCalEval is the first benchmark that quantitatively evaluates how well vision–language models interpret quantum calibration plots, exposing specific strengths and weaknesses across diverse experimental scenarios.
problem_solved: Addresses the absence of a systematic evaluation for VLM understanding of calibration plots used in quantum experiments — a critical gap for automating interpretation and troubleshooting in quantum labs.
method: Curated dataset: 243 annotated calibration plots covering 87 scenario types from 22 experiment families (including superconducting qubits and neutral atoms).
Task design: six question types that probe visual, numerical and conceptual understanding of calibration plots, evaluated in zero-/few-shot settings.
Evaluation: standardized metrics and per-task analyses to quantify VLM performance and identify common failure modes.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a targeted benchmark to measure and improve VLMs on scientific figure understanding, guiding model development for lab-assistive tools and automated calibration pipelines.
visual_elements: Annotated example calibration plot with callouts for key features (peaks, baselines, fit parameters).
Bar chart showing accuracy per question type to highlight strengths and weaknesses.
Heatmap of error rates by experiment family and scenario type to reveal domain gaps.
Dataset composition infographic (counts by experiment family, scenario types, and total samples).
paper_title: QCalEval: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Quantum Calibration Plot Understanding
paper_authors: Shuxiang Cao, Zijian Zhang, Abhishek Agarwal, Grace Bratrud, Niyaz R. Beysengulov
